sharon: Heads-up: saw a ~2.4x tail-latency regression on mixtral-8k after the tokenizer update on prod. Symptoms: spikes on requests with chat templates and a particular system prompt that includes non-ascii emojis.

sharon: Quick sample numbers from canary yesterday: p95 went from 120ms -> 290ms for identical workload. CPU/GPU utilization unchanged.

perf-bot: Automated profiling attached: kernel_fallback_count=1342, kv_cache_evictions=412, avg_seq_len_tokens=98, avg_token_bytes=1.7

sharon: I suspect byte-fallback/tokenizer behavior -> more tokens -> worse batching and more KV thrashing.

jen: Can you paste the tokenization diff? We recently added unicode normalization to avoid unknown tokens, maybe that's causing multi-byte token expansion.

sharon: snippet: ``apply_normalizer = True`` was flipped and we added a fallback to byte-level for characters not in vocab.

sharon: Example: old tokenization for message A = 42 tokens, new tokenization = 73 tokens. Same raw text.

todd: If seq_len distribution shifts right, our dynamic batcher will try to pack more short + one long into same batch -> KV cache reinitialization while longer sequence dominates. Also kernel selector may pick dense attention kernels suboptimal for long tail.

raj: From infra traces: many requests fell back to the generic attention kernel (fallback_kernel_id=0x7a) instead of model-optimized one (0x3b) when seq_len>256. Kernel selection rule currently: if seq_len_blocking=true OR detected_token_type=byte_fallback -> choose generic.

jen: That matches: byte_fallback flag is set when normalizer changes produce unknown subwords. But why would it trigger generic kernel? Should be orthogonal. Looks like we gate optimized kernels on token_type == 'subword' which is naive.

todd: Profiling stack (short):
```
- dispatch -> select_kernel(seq_len, model_arch, token_type)
- kernel_exec(optimized_attn_v2)  // fast path
- fallback -> generic_attn // slow path
```

todd: Two fixes we can try: a) relax token_type check so optimized kernels selected by seq_len+heads/kv dims, b) make batcher bucket by "effective token load" = tokens * avg_token_bytes to avoid mixing heavy byte-fallback requests with normal ones.

sharon: I ran a quick experiment switching kernel selection to ignore token_type; p95 dropped to ~140ms on canary. But we saw correctness concerns on qwen-34B variants (rotary / RoPE scaling mismatch).

jen: Right — RoPE scaling interacts with head_dim and kv layout. If we pick an optimized kernel compiled for rotary_scale=1.0 but model expects 1.3, results diverge. So kernel selection can't be purely perf-based; we must match kernel metadata (roPE, head_dim, kv_dim).

raj: Suggest adding per-model kernel metadata checks into selector: kernel metadata = {arch, head_dim, kv_dim, rope_scale, quant_scheme}. Selector should check compatibility first, then resource heuristics.

sharon: Agreed. For immediate mitigation: 1) revert unicode normalizer flip for hosted API stable tier; 2) change batcher to bucket by effective_token_load; 3) add kernel selector compatibility checks to avoid RoPE mismatch.

todd: Also saw a pattern where BOS/EOS handling in chat templates added an extra special token on both system and assistant messages, causing token_count variance. Those extra tokens push some requests over 256 boundary and trigger slower kernels. We should normalize templates to avoid duplicate special tokens.

jen: For model-specific tuning: Mixtral needs head_dim remap in our quant kernels (its kv dims are 128 vs 96 expected). We'll add a fallback mapping layer that remaps kv layout at compile time instead of using generic kernel. That should reduce generic fallbacks.

sharon: I'll open a canary PR with these changes: batching buckets + token_type ignore for optimized kernels + revert normalizer on stable. Can we also add a small telemetry flag to capture "effective_token_load" per request?

raj: Yes, I'll expose effective_token_load in request trace and a feature flag to record it for 1% traffic. Add it to TraceEvent: `trace.eff_load` (float).

todd: Quick note on quantization: when we switch kernels we need to check per-head scaling. Mismatched per-head quant scales cause small numeric drift that can flip top-k in some cases. Add eval harness check when a kernel switch happens: run a deterministic prompt set and compare token logits.

jen: Sounds good. Also let's patch tokenizer to coalesce sequences of special tokens and mark them so batching can treat them as 1 logical token for batching heuristics (not for model input, just for pack sizing). Reduces harmful bucket mixing.

sharon: Action items:
- sharon: revert normalizer on stable API + open PR for canary changes (batcher + kernel selector)
- raj: telemetry flag + trace field
- todd: compile metadata checks + eval harness hook for kernel swaps
- jen: tokenizer coalescing + investigate mixtral kv layout remap

jen: I'll also add a short eval: run 10k chat prompts with emojis and measure token_count delta and kernel_fallback_count before/after. Post results in this thread.

sharon: Thanks — let's aim to roll the canary tonight and monitor p95 & correctness. If anyone sees production noise after the revert ping me @sharon. :thumbsup:
